records.title: Minefield laid

fields.event: (5th Contact) (1st Attack) Lat. 35-45 N. Long. 140-55 E. 8400 ton freighter Sunk by Mines. Sighted a ship approaching from the southward heading almost exactly for this vessel. Ceased laying mines. Intended to permit this vessel to go by and then resume laying mines. Vessel was now identified as a large freighter with a small escort vessel inshore from it. They passed under our stern, this vessel on course 090 at that time. Position could have been perfect for a torpedo attack with stern tubes but considered completion of the mine plant as the immediate objective. A bit over five minutes after the freighter passed our stern, there was a violent explosion.

flags: target sunk by mines during mine laying

fields.event: The freighter is 90 degrees from her former course lying in the trough of the seas rolling in the heavy swells violently while the escort vessel is circling her. An excellent view of the freighter was now had. Her back had been broken. Amidships the main deck was awash. About ten feet of the stern was above water and the bow was high out of water. The freighter sank rapidly. She had a raked bow, cruiser or counter stern, composite superstructure, flush deck except for a slight forecastle, one squat stack, masts, etc., not seen. Her appearance was similar to the following Marus: AIKOKU, KINRYU, HIROKAWA, KANSAI, KASII, CANBERRA, KYUSU, SADO, the average tonnage of which is 8400. She was making about 15 knots. The escort vessel appeared to be a motor torpedo boat. The presence of this escort, the first of the vessels sighted off INUBO SAKI with an escort, indicated the high value of the ship. Decided that there would probably be anti-submarine vessels in the vicinity at once so commenced retirement into deep water. We were in fifteen fathoms of water with a considerable distance to go before deep submergence would be possible.
Another violent explosion. Nothing seen. Possibly another mine caught someone, perhaps the escort vessel.
[SUMMARY] Screws picked up by sound; went deep and rigged for silent running and depth charge attack; evasion tactics successful.
Surfaced and cleared the area at high speed.
Sighted a huge cloud of smoke from the mine fields.
On station on course line 312 to NOJIMA SAKI to intercept traffic from the southeast.
Surfaced and headed for NOJIMA SAKI at high speed to be off this point close in for the coming day's observation.
Commenced patrol off NOJIMA SAKI.

records.title: Torpedo attack (narrative)

fields.event: Fired a spread of torpedoes on 90 track just as she steadied on a left zig. The spread used was speed spread using the diagram recently issued by ComSubPac; one torpedo at least to hit. One torpedo hit was made just forward of the bridge. She immediately started down by the bow, tooting her whistle and turning away. We were at that time in shallow water about two miles off-shore bearing 240 from NOJIMA SAKI with the current setting us on therefore about to go aground, so turned

records.title: Torpedo attack (narrative)

fields.event: (6th Contact) (2nd Attack) Lat. 34-52 N. Long. 139-49 E. 5000 ton freighter sunk. Sighted smoke up in URAGA SUIDO. As vessel approached, made it out to be a freighter zigzagging on about 60 degree legs. This vessel was in position to attack regardless of whether the destination of the target is north or southeast.
